safeguards: The current committed YAML uses 3.0 Hz and the shared validator rejects nonfinite, negative or zero frequency/half-life and transmission above one. The example is not a claim about shipped default behavior.

candidates.severity: unassigned; conditional nonfinite client presentation state
candidates.classification: New bounded current validated-configuration to spring-operation trace, connected to the earlier explicitly open numeric question.
candidates.trace: BouncyBonesConfig uses f32 leaves and the shared TacticalCombatConfig validator accepts any finite nonnegative frequency greater than zero; it imposes no upper frequency bound. Assuming all other fields pass validation, a configuration whose frequency_hz is f32::MAX meets that frequency check and can be installed through the validated runtime snapshot. spring_step multiplies it by the finite positive TAU, producing positive infinity under the preserved Rust f32 overflow contract before computing damped frequency and sin_cos. With a zero-offset, finite-nonzero-velocity spring and positive frame delta, the later spring.offset * damped includes zero times infinity; the operation can produce NaN and there is no finite check before the newly computed spring is stored. The spring is client-only presentation; the committed YAML frequency is 3.0 Hz, not the extreme example. No alternate configuration was installed, no hit occurred and no animation ran.
candidates.guards_and_limits: The active system skips at-rest springs and nonpositive frame time, and the event producer requires a nonzero hit velocity. Offsets are clamped after the step; the transform walk applies an offset only when its squared length exceeds a threshold, so a NaN comparison does not itself demonstrate a NaN transform. Ragdolled or frozen rigs skip the transform walk. Exact platform trigonometry, glam operations, actual poisoned state persistence, observation and visual effect remain open. The separate `sin_cos` behavior at infinity is not assumed to be identical across all Rust targets.
candidates.connected_repair: Make the shared validated server-supplied tuning and every spring transition preserve finite representable state: check relevant intermediate arithmetic or reject unrepresentable configuration at its owning shared admission, then prepare a complete finite spring update before replacing retained state. Preserve normal half-life, frequency, coupling, hit response, zero/rest behavior, frozen and ragdoll policy, and avoid adding client-local fallback tuning or hidden gameplay effects.
candidates.later_acceptance: Only after separate implementation and product-validation authorization, cover a valid ordinary tuning and hit, large-but-finite tuning, zero/rest and finite extreme cases with controlled time, and the project-required native diagnostic for any live tactical defect.
candidates.discovery: partial; supported authored extreme policy, hit/state construction, platform math and all spring producers/consumers, exact aliases and live presentation remain open

remaining: Admitted non-default configuration and spring state reachability, platform math, server/client synchronization, asset revisions, live visual consequences, exact aliases and all independent lenses remain open. Final checkpoint 3821 ledger and queue remain missing.
